episodes.title: Why Making Your Kids Obey Backfires | Heather Jessup
episodes.description:
🌮 Want early access, uncut moments & full archive? Join us on Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=youtube

Heather Jessup is a former teacher who now says gold stars and behavior charts don't work for every kid. Some kids have PDA, a profile of autism where everyday requests, even "let's go get ice cream," can feel to their nervous system like being hunted by an apex predator.

We asked her whether our own son's meltdowns are PDA, why she believes some people are in prison because of it, what to tell 911 dispatch before police show up, why some families take chores and showers off the table, and why she says connection beats compliance.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Heather Jessup is a Certified PDA Trainer and the chairperson and co-founder of Journeys With PDA, a new 501(c)(3) that offers free support chats, family education and family consulting. She co-hosts the Journeys With PDA Coffee Chat Podcast and was diagnosed with ADHD later in life.

episodes.title: Cult Expert: The Craving That Gets You Recruited
episodes.description:
Janice Selbie spent 18 years married to a pastor. She wore a head covering, no makeup and no jewelry, and homeschooled her kids. Now she helps people recover from religion, and she says anyone can fall for a guru, even nuclear physicists.

We sat down with her to talk about the craving every human has that makes us easy to recruit, why so many people who escape one cult end up in an MLM, the demon that can fly up your nose if nobody says "God bless you" fast enough, and the apology letters she wrote her daughters after she left.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Janice Selbie, RPC, is a religious trauma recovery coach, professional speaker and the author of the bestsellers Divorcing Religion and The Guru Gene. She founded the Conference on Religious Trauma (CORT) and Shameless Sexuality: Life After Purity Culture, and hosts the Divorcing Religion and Sex and Power podcasts.

episodes.title: Her Bishop Punished Her. Her Boyfriend Got a Pass. | Mellissa Perry Hill
episodes.description: Mellissa Perry Hill was a divorced single mom of three when she confessed to her bishop. He took her temple recommend and told her she couldn't take the sacrament, with her kids sitting right next to her. The man she was dating confessed to his bishop too. He was told to keep trying. Mellissa grew up mainstream Mormon, spent ten years as a stay at home mom, and walked out of church the day her kids cried the whole way there. We sat down with her to talk about why her ward wanted her remarried instead of in grad school, why she helps women become a little more narcissistic, what watching Sister Wives showed her about her own church, and the temple vow that left her furious. Mellissa Perry Hill, MS, LPC, is a psychotherapist who specializes in religious trauma. She works with active, former, and questioning members of the LDS church and other high control groups, and sees clients in Arizona and Utah. episodes.title: Stay-at-Home Daughter Was Raised to Be Handed to a Husband | Katherine Spearing, Author
episodes.description: Katherine Spearing was 24 years old when her dad banned her from driving or leaving the house for two weeks. Her crime? Hanging up on him while he was yelling at her. Katherine was a stay-at-home daughter, raised in the Christian patriarchy movement to live under her father's roof and authority until she could be passed to a husband's. No college, no career, no car. She didn't get out until she was 26. We sat down with her to talk about how a dad builds his own little cult inside a family, why it attracts the men it does, control that comes with a smile, and what it really takes to leave. Katherine is an author and the founder of Tears of Eden, a resource hub and community for survivors of spiritual abuse. After leaving her father's home, she spent eight years in full-time church ministry before founding nonprofits for survivors of abuse. Her book, A Thousand Tiny Paper Cuts: The Subtle Insidious Nature of Spiritual Abuse and Life on the Other Side, uses her own story to explain what spiritual abuse looks like and how to heal from it. 🌮 Early access, uncut moments and Patreon-only content with Mykelti, for the price of one taco a month: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=podcast Watch our interviews on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@tacoboutitpod Follow Mykelti: IG @mykeltip · TikTok @mykeltipadron Follow Tony: IG @tonychessnut · TikTok @tonychessnut12 Follow Katherine: IG @katherinespearing · katherinespearing.com · Book: A Thousand Tiny Paper Cuts Taco 'Bout It is a podcast at the intersection of tacos, tea, and trauma, hosted by Mykelti Brown Padron and Tony Padron. episodes.title: You Were Raised to Be Submissive and Never Knew | Religious Trauma Therapist | Krispin Mayfield
episodes.description: Krispin Mayfield spent years in ministry and wrote a Christian book before leaving the faith. Now he's explaining why so many of us were trained to obey before we were ever allowed to feel. Mykelti grew up in a plural family on national TV, and Tony grew up in the Mormon church. Both were taught that obedience mattered more than anything, and both still see it in how they make decisions and raise their own kids. So we sat down with a religious trauma therapist to ask the big question: was it discipline, or was it abuse? Krispin is a licensed professional counselor in Oregon and the author of Attached to God. He co-writes Strongwilled, a Substack about healing from religious authoritarian parenting. We talk about why high-control religion puts obedience above everything, why so many adults still can't answer "where do you want to eat?", the popular baby book millions of parents trusted that was secretly Christian, the preacher who first told London's orphans their hearts were black with sin, Krispin's Christian screamo era, whether spanking was discipline or abuse, and what to do instead if you see yourself in this. These are Krispin's professional and personal opinions. This isn't about shaming parents who did what they thought was right. It's about understanding how these patterns get passed down so we can stop passing them on. 🌮 Early access, uncut moments and Patreon-only content with Mykelti, for the price of one taco a month: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=podcast Watch our interviews on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@tacoboutitpod Follow Mykelti: IG @mykeltip · TikTok @mykeltipadron Follow Tony: IG @tonychessnut · TikTok @tonychessnut12 Follow Krispin: Krispin Mayfield on Instagram · Strongwilled on Substack · Book: Attached to God Taco 'Bout It is a podcast at the intersection of tacos, tea, and trauma, hosted by Mykelti Brown Padron and Tony Padron. episodes.title: Sister Wives & Mormon Purity Culture: A Therapist Reviews the Damage | Dr. Camden Morgante
episodes.description: Mykelti's dad once told a boy on Sister Wives that kissing her would put his hormones in her mouth. Now a psychologist finally weighs in. Mykelti grew up in a plural family on national TV. Tony grew up in the Mormon church. Both were taught that purity was everything, and both are still unpacking what that did to them, to their marriage, and to how they're raising their own kids. So we sat down with Dr. Camden Morgante, a licensed clinical psychologist, former college professor and author of Recovering from Purity Culture. Raised evangelical, she wore a True Love Waits ring for ten years before she started researching the damage purity culture leaves behind. We talk about the "hormones in your mouth" talk and what the science actually says, whether what a girl wears really makes assault more likely, the "damaged goods" myth and why she calls it the most harmful one, the "flip switch" myth and what it did to our early marriage, how to talk to kids about sex without passing down the shame, and what purity culture does to men. This isn't about bashing anyone's faith. It's about what happens when shame becomes the lesson, and how you start to unlearn it. 🌮 Early access, uncut moments and Patreon-only content with Mykelti, for the price of one taco a month: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=podcast Watch our interviews on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@tacoboutitpod Follow Mykelti: IG @mykeltip · TikTok @mykeltipadron Follow Tony: IG @tonychessnut · TikTok @tonychessnut12 Dr. Camden's book: Recovering from Purity Culture (the audiobook is read by her) Taco 'Bout It is a podcast at the intersection of tacos, tea, and trauma, hosted by Mykelti Brown Padron and Tony Padron. episodes.title: The Vow's NXIVM Whistleblower: Why She Couldn't Leave | Sarah Edmondson
episodes.description: Sarah Edmondson joined NXIVM looking for a supportive community, and within a few years she was one of its top recruiters. Then came a brand she was told was a tattoo, blackmail collateral, and a lifetime vow of obedience. Now she uses everything she learned about how recruitment really works to help other people see it coming. Sarah is one of the central voices in HBO's The Vow, co-host of the A Little Bit Culty podcast, and co-author with her husband Anthony "Nippy" Ames of A Little Bit Culty: Navigating Cults, Control and Coercion. Her memoir Scarred traces her path into NXIVM and back out. We talk about recruiting people into NXIVM and eventually being recruited into DOS herself, the brand and what it cost her, the blackmail structure that made leaving so hard, why "why didn't you just leave" misses the point, how she learned to trust her gut again after years of gaslighting, and what it's like being recognized from The Vow everywhere she goes. This isn't just a true crime story. It's about how slowly coercion can be built into something that looks like self-improvement, until it owns you. 🌮 Early access, uncut moments and Patreon-only content with Mykelti, for the price of one taco a month: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=podcast Watch our interviews on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@tacoboutitpod Follow Mykelti: IG @mykeltip · TikTok @mykeltipadron Follow Tony: IG @tonychessnut · TikTok @tonychessnut12 Follow Sarah: Sarah Edmondson on Instagram · A Little Bit Culty, wherever you get podcasts Taco 'Bout It is a podcast at the intersection of tacos, tea, and trauma, hosted by Mykelti Brown Padron and Tony Padron. episodes.title: The TikToker Whose Family Was Almost Broken by Fundamentalism | Ex-Evangelical | April Ajoy
episodes.description: April Ajoy grew up certain her family was 100% right about everything. Then an exorcism, her father's death, and a decade of that certainty nearly cost her the people she loved most. Now she uses the exact tool that raised her, persuasion, for the opposite job: disarming people with jokes instead of convincing them with arguments. April is an author, a TikTok creator with 430K followers, and co-host of The Tim and April Show, known for her satirical takes on the Christian nationalist movement she was raised in. Her book Star-Spangled Jesus traces how she left that movement without leaving her faith, and she's featured in Shiny Happy People. We talk about the exorcism her now-husband Beecher performed, what it costs a family to believe it's always right, her father's death and a question she still hasn't fully answered about blame, and why jokes became her whole career. This isn't about her politics. It's about what happens when "we're the ones who are right" becomes the whole foundation of a family. 🌮 Early access, uncut moments and Patreon-only content with Mykelti, for the price of one taco a month: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=podcast Watch our interviews on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@tacoboutitpod Follow Mykelti: IG @mykeltip · TikTok @mykeltipadron Follow Tony: IG @tonychessnut · TikTok @tonychessnut12 Follow April: @aprilajoy pretty much everywhere · Book: Star-Spangled Jesus Taco 'Bout It is a podcast at the intersection of tacos, tea, and trauma, hosted by Mykelti Brown Padron and Tony Padron. episodes.title: If Your Church Did This, It Was Abuse | Therapist Anna Clark Miller
episodes.description: Anna Clark Miller spent years working in a domestic violence shelter. Then she started treating people coming out of high-control religion, and noticed that the tool counselors use to explain how abusers control their partners described what she was hearing from church survivors almost exactly. So she rebuilt it. We asked her how much she actually had to change. Her answer: barely anything. Anna is a licensed therapist specializing in religious trauma and the founder of Empathy Paradigm. She walks us through her adaptation of the Power and Control Wheel, spoke by spoke, and we test it against our own upbringings along the way, including Mykelti's in the AUB. We get into being told to pull up her bank statements in front of her church group, 20 hours a week of unpaid worship leading, the question she's never fully answered about harm you cause while you're being deceived yourself, and why her body still reacts to worship music years after leaving. This isn't about calling your church abusive. episodes.title: Raised Polygamist, Now I Believe in Reincarnation.
episodes.description:
🌮 Want early access, uncut moments & full archive? Join us on Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=youtube

Mykelti believes she's lived before. Not as a metaphor — she thinks this is not her first time here. Tony thinks the whole idea makes the universe worse. No guest this week, no expert to settle it. Just the two of us and the biggest thing we've never agreed on.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Neither of us has a theology degree. Neither of us is going to pretend otherwise. What we do have is two completely different ways of looking at the same unanswerable question — and about an hour of going at it.

We cover:

Why the first law of thermodynamics is the foundation of Mykelti's whole belief
The University of Virginia researcher who spent decades documenting children who remembered dying as someone else
Whether being reborn as a cow would be a second chance or a prison
Tony's math problem: if souls get recycled, there are fewer of them
Why karma only seems to punish and never pay out
Whether "I'd rather believe this" is a good enough reason to believe anything
The moment Mykelti turns Tony's own Mormon upbringing back on him

Nobody wins. That was never the point.

episodes.title: Mormon Polygamy Didn't Start the Way You Were Told | Benjamin Park
episodes.description: Mykelti grew up polygamist, and she was always taught it started with a revelation from God. So we sat down with a historian who has spent his career inside the actual archives, and who is also a believing Latter-day Saint writing unflinchingly about his own church's history. Almost nothing lines up the way we were taught. Dr. Benjamin Park is an Associate Professor of History at Sam Houston State University, Past President of the Mormon History Association, and the author of American Zion: A New History of Mormonism and Kingdom of Nauvoo, the definitive scholarly account of where Mormon polygamy began. We talk about where polygamy actually started, years before the revelation that was supposed to justify it, why that revelation was written to convince one woman, Emma Smith, the teenage girls, secret sealings and the women who said no, and how the revelation stayed hidden until Brigham Young made it public in 1852. episodes.title: I Grew Up Polygamist. I Asked a Bible Scholar If God Approved. | Dr. Robert Gnuse
episodes.description: Mykelti grew up polygamist, and the justification was always the Bible: Abraham, Jacob, David, Solomon. So we finally sat down with someone who could actually check, a scholar with a doctorate in the Old Testament who has spent 46 years reading the text in its original languages. Almost nothing he told us matches what we were taught. Dr. Robert Gnuse is a Distinguished Professor of the Humanities at Loyola University New Orleans, holds a Ph.D. from Vanderbilt, and has written 12 books on the Bible. He was an ordained Lutheran minister and still preaches on Sundays. We ask him whether the Bible endorses polygamy, describes it or condemns it, what plural households like Sarah and Hagar or Rachel and Leah actually looked like, what really happened with Solomon's thousand wives, what Adam and Eve's real sin was, what Sodom and Leviticus actually say, whether women led the early church, and the retranslation of "wives, submit to your husbands" that changes everything. episodes.title: Chess.com Exec Reveals the Cult That Took Him at 12 | Danny Rensch
episodes.description: He learned chess at 10. By 12 he was one of the highest-rated kids in the country, and that's when a spirit channeled through a trance medium declared that chess was his purpose. The same doctrine said that purpose outranked his own mother. We sat down with Danny Rensch, Chief Chess Officer at Chess.com and author of the memoir Dark Squares, to talk about growing up inside a spiritual collective. We get into why people followed its leaders, "the process" and how shame kept everyone in line, being put on the hot seat as a kid for losing at chess, the room where he agreed to leave his mother, building Chess.com while still inside the collective, EMDR and ten years of therapy, and losing his mom before the reconciliation was finished. He's unusually honest about the parts that don't make a clean redemption arc. episodes.title: Therapist: You Left Church but Your Body Didn't | Ashley Buckner
episodes.description: You can leave the church, do the work, move across the country, and still carry it in your body. Ashley Buckner grew up Mormon, left at 20, and became a therapist who specializes in the one thing talk therapy keeps missing: where trauma actually lives, and how to get it out. We sat down with Ashley to talk about religious trauma, the nervous system, and a body-based technique called brain spotting. We get into why leaving a high-control religion can code as trauma in your body, "eternal families" and the cost of conditional love, why speaking out gets you targeted, why not everyone is owed access to you, even family, and the body-based therapies worth looking into if you want to start healing. It's a warm, funny, surprisingly hopeful conversation about where trauma hides and the therapy almost no one talks about. 🌮 Early access, uncut moments and Patreon-only content with Mykelti, for the price of one taco a month: https://www.patreon.com/cw/mykelti?utm_source=podcast Watch our interviews on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@tacoboutitpod Follow Mykelti: IG @mykeltip · TikTok @mykeltipadron Follow Tony: IG @tonychessnut · TikTok @tonychessnut12 Follow Ashley: Ashley Buckner on Instagram and TikTok Taco 'Bout It is a podcast at the intersection of tacos, tea, and trauma, hosted by Mykelti Brown Padron and Tony Padron. episodes.title: He Grew Up FLDS in Short Creek — We're Unpacking Netflix's "Trust Me: The False Prophet"
episodes.description: He was a nobody. Then he had wives, kids, and a community calling him a prophet. How does an ordinary man in Short Creek convince anyone he speaks for God, and why couldn't anyone stop him? We sat down with Sam and Melissa from Growing Up in Polygamy to break down the Netflix series "Trust Me: The False Prophet" and the real story behind Samuel Bateman. Sam grew up FLDS in Short Creek, minutes from where it all happened, and Bateman is family. We talk about how Warren Jeffs left behind exactly the kind of men Bateman could exploit, the "translated, not dead" claim Bateman used to speak for an imprisoned Warren Jeffs, why law enforcement waited so long, who comes next once Warren is gone, and whether the next prophet could be powered by AI. episodes.description: What happens when the church you were raised in starts watching your every move, and the only way out is to stop performing for everyone but yourself? We sat down with Jessica (@jazzika), an ex-Mormon TikTok storyteller and one of the funniest, most unfiltered voices in the deconstruction space. episodes.title: Kicked Out at 16, Now an Atheist Spiritual Director | Britt Hartley
episodes.description: Britt Hartley was kicked out of her Mormon home at 16. Years later, she lost her faith completely while studying theology. What if the most damaging patriarchy isn't the kind that hates women — 
but the kind that calls them angels?

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

In this episode of Taco 'Bout It, Mykelti and Tony sit down with 
Amy McPhee Allebest — host of Breaking Down Patriarchy and Stanford-
educated historian who spent years researching how patriarchal systems 
actually function — to talk about the difference between the patriarchy 
that hates women and the patriarchy that loves them too much.

We cover:
- How "benevolent patriarchy" hides inside kindness, chivalry & 
  religious devotion
- Why being called "an angel" might be the most disempowering 
  compliment of all
- The Yale professor who said studying women was like "writing the 
  history of dogs"
- The viral "Dear Mormon Man" essay — and what it reveals about 
  gender flipping

This one breaks down a system most of us have lived inside without 
ever naming .
